subject: Evaluation onramp: environment gating, API keys & peering next steps
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cardiotech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cardiotech.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation onramp: environment gating, API keys & peering next steps

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed by the latency numbers and the rollback options. We're ready to move into a short evaluation but need a concrete plan for the technical gating so our infra and security teams can sign off. Specifically we need: 

- Org setup guidance (single org vs. multiple projects)
- Scoped API keys and rotation policies
- IP allowlist definition and expected egress ranges
- VPC peering requirements (route tables, CIDR expectations, and whether NAT is required)

Would you be able to send a short mutual action plan and a target close timeline for the evaluation phase (2–3 week window preferred)? We also have a procurement checklist that will need a DocuSign for the MSA if we move forward.

Appreciate it — Sara

Sara Kim
Director, Product Integrations
CardioTech
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cardiotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation onramp: environment gating, API keys & peering next steps

Hi Sara — great to hear the demo landed well. Attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP_CardioTech_v1.xlsx) that breaks the evaluation into three milestone sprints across 18 days. Highlights below: 

1) Org & access (Day 0–2): we recommend a single Redwood org with two projects (dev/eval). We provide a bootstrap script to create scoped service accounts; Marissa will share the script and a one-pager.

2) API keys (Day 1–4): scoped API keys with least privilege. Keys are issued via the console; rotation guidance included in the MAP. We recommend short-lived keys for the eval (12–24h) plus a token cache policy to reduce reauths.

3) Network (Day 2–8): IP allowlist for control plane (we'll share specific IPs). For VPC peering we support both native peering and VPN transit. If you want private egress for inference traffic, plan for a SNAT/NAT gateway — we call this out in the network draft (cardiotech-network-draft.pdf).

4) Compliance & procurement (Day 8–18): procurement collects minimal items listed in the MAP; we can provide SOC2 artifact pointers. DocuSign link included for the intake sheet.

Next steps I propose: Marissa will kick off the environment bootstrap on Wednesday, Ben will coordinate the procurement/DocuSign flow, and I will share the IP allowlist and a short runbook for verifying peering. Can you confirm your infra point-of-contact so we can schedule the peering window?

Attachments: MAP_CardioTech_v1.xlsx (action items + timeline), cardiotech-network-draft.pdf (network specifics), docusign-intake-link.url

Best,
Logan Wright
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation onramp: environment gating, API keys & peering next steps

Looping in the bootstrap details — Logan, I've attached the quickstart bootstrap script and a one-pager to the shared Drive link. Summary of what I'll run with the CardioTech infra team: 

- Create Redwood org with eval project + scoped roles (read-only monitoring + inference submit)
- Generate two short-lived service keys: evaluator-key-1 (12h) and ci-key (24h)
- Provide a verification snippet (curl) so their infra team can confirm allowlist connectivity before peering

Ben — please initiate the DocuSign intake and confirm the procurement contact. Sarah (procurement) mentioned they'd prefer to sign the intake before peering. I recommend we schedule the peering maintenance window for Day 4 after allowlist verification.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: bootstrap.sh (script), bootstrap-onepager.md (in Drive)
